arguments.content:
---
name: slack-api
description: "Interact with the Slack Web API to send, read, update, and delete messages; post to channels and threads; list and search channels and conversations; list and look up users; manage reactions; upload files; and verify tokens. Use whenever the user asks to post to Slack, read Slack history, list Slack channels or members, add emoji reactions, search Slack, or perform any other operation against api.slack.com with a bot or user token."
---

# Slack API

Interact with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API (`https://slack.com/api/`).

## Prerequisites

- A Slack token with the scopes required by the endpoints you use. Bot tokens (`xoxb-...`) are preferred; user tokens (`xoxp-...`) are needed for some user-level operations.
- Provide the token as the `SLACK_TOKEN` (or `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`) environment variable, or pass it explicitly with the helper script's `--token` flag.

## Core workflow

1. **Choose an endpoint.** See [references/api.md](references/api.md) for the full endpoint reference (params, scopes, examples). Common picks:
   - Send a message: `chat.postMessage`
   - Read a channel's history: `conversations.history`
   - List channels: `conversations.list`
   - List users: `users.list`
   - Add a reaction: `reactions.add`
   - Search messages: `search.messages`

2. **Call the API.** The base URL is `https://slack.com/api/`. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and JSON bodies with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every method works as GET or POST; use POST for writes.

   ```bash
   # curl
   curl -sS -X POST "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Hello from an agent!"}'

   # or the bundled helper script
   node scripts/slack_request.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Hello from an agent!"}'
   ```

3. **Check the response envelope.** Every response is JSON with an `ok` boolean. If `ok` is `false`, read the `error` field and fix the cause:
   - `not_authed` / `invalid_auth` — missing or bad token
   - `missing_scope` — token lacks the required scope; add it and reinstall the app
   - `channel_not_found` — bad channel ID (IDs look like `C...`, `D...`, `G...`); resolve names with `conversations.list`
   - `invalid_arguments` — see `response_metadata.messages` for details

4. **Paginate.** List endpoints return at most 100–200 items per call. Follow `response_metadata.next_cursor` by passing it as the `cursor` parameter until it is empty. The helper script does this automatically with `--paginate`.

5. **Respect rate limits.** Slack returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header when throttled. Honor it before retrying; the helper script retries automatically (3 attempts by default).

## Helper script

`scripts/slack_request.cjs` is a thin CLI over the Web API: it handles auth, JSON encoding/parsing, 429 retries, and optional cursor pagination, and prints a concise LLM-friendly summary (never a raw traceback).

```bash
node scripts/slack_request.cjs api.test
node scripts/slack_request.cjs conversations.list --paginate --max-pages 5
node scripts/slack_request.cjs users.info '{"user":"U1234567890"}'
node scripts/slack_request.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"#general","text":"hi"}' --token xoxb-...
```

Run `node scripts/slack_request.cjs --help` for all options.

## Notes

- Slack IDs are opaque strings: `C...` channel, `D...` DM, `G...` group/MPIM, `U...` user, `B...` bot. Prefer IDs over names when an endpoint requires them.
- `files.upload` uses `multipart/form-data`, not JSON — see [references/api.md](references/api.md).
- For complex multi-step workflows, prefer the official SDKs (`@slack/web-api` in Node, `slack_sdk` in Python) over raw HTTP.
- Full endpoint reference, error catalog, and rate-limit details: [references/api.md](references/api.md).

# Slack Web API Reference

Companion to SKILL.md. Covers authentication, response handling, rate limits, pagination, and the endpoints most commonly needed for agent workflows.

## Contents

1. [Authentication & scopes](#authentication--scopes)
2. [Response envelope](#response-envelope)
3. [Errors](#errors)
4. [Rate limits](#rate-limits)
5. [Pagination](#pagination)
6. [Messages](#messages)
7. [Conversations & channels](#conversations--channels)
8. [Users](#users)
9. [Reactions](#reactions)
10. [Files](#files)
11. [Search](#search)
12. [Workspace & token checks](#workspace--token-checks)
13. [SDKs](#sdks)

## Authentication & scopes

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/`. All methods are HTTP GET or POST; POST is accepted everywhere and required for writes.
- Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; bot tokens start with `xoxb-`, user tokens with `xoxp-`.
- Scopes are granted per token (bot scopes for `xoxb-`, user scopes for `xoxp-`). The endpoint tables below list the scope typically required. `missing_scope` errors mean the token lacks the scope; add it in the app settings and reinstall the app.
- Method names map directly to URLs: `chat.postMessage` -> `https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage`.

## Response envelope

Every endpoint returns JSON with an `ok` field:

- `{"ok": true, ...}` — success; payload fields vary per method.
- `{"ok": false, "error": "channel_not_found", ...}` — failure; the `error` string is the machine-readable cause. `invalid_arguments` responses also include `response_metadata.messages` with human-readable details.

Always check `ok` before using payload fields.

## Errors

Common `error` values:

| error | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `not_authed` | No token was sent |
| `invalid_auth` | Token is malformed or revoked |
| `account_inactive` | Workspace is deactivated |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks the required scope |
| `invalid_arguments` | Bad parameters; see `response_metadata.messages` |
| `channel_not_found` | Channel/thread ID not found (IDs: `C...` channel, `D...` DM, `G...` group/MPIM) |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived; unarchive before posting |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot/user is not a member of the channel |
| `name_taken` | Channel name already exists |
| `invalid_name` | Channel name is invalid |
| `user_not_found` | User ID not found |
| `already_reacted` | Reaction already added by this user |
| `no_reaction` | Reaction does not exist (removal failed) |
| `rate_limited` | HTTP 429; see below |
| `internal_error` | Transient Slack-side failure; retry |

## Rate limits

- Limits are per-method and tiered (Tier 1 is the lowest, Tier 4 the highest). Sustained throughput above a tier's limit returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header (seconds).
- Honor `Retry-After` before retrying. The helper script does this automatically (3 attempts by default).
- Some endpoints have extra protections (e.g., `conversations.history`); batch reads with `--paginate` and add small sleeps between heavy loops.

## Pagination

- List-style endpoints return `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Pass it back as the `cursor` parameter to fetch the next page; an empty string means the end was reached.
- Default page sizes are 100–200 items; use `limit` where supported.
- The helper script follows cursors automatically with `--paginate` and caps pages with `--max-pages`.

## Messages

| method | scope | key params | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.postMessage` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `text` or `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `mrkdwn`, `link_names`, `unfurl_links` | Send a message. Returns `ts` + `channel`. |
| `chat.update` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `ts`, `text`/`blocks` | Edit a message by its timestamp. |
| `chat.delete` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `ts` | Delete a message. |
| `chat.postEphemeral` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `user`, `text` | Message visible only to one user. |
| `chat.scheduleMessage` | `chat:write` | `channel`, `text`, `post_at` | `post_at` is a Unix timestamp. |
| `chat.getPermalink` | none | `channel`, `message_ts` | Permanent link to a message. |
| `conversations.history` | `channels:history` etc. | `channel`, `limit`, `cursor`, `oldest`, `latest` | Message history (newest first). |
| `conversations.replies` | `channels:history` etc. | `channel`, `ts` | All replies in a thread. |

Formatting: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `<@U123|name>` mentions, `<#C123|channel>` channel links, `<https://example.com|label>` links. Block Kit JSON goes in `blocks`.

## Conversations & channels

| method | scope | key params | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `conversations.list` | `channels:read` | `types` (`public_channel,private_channel,mpim,im`), `limit`, `cursor`, `exclude_archived` | List channels; resolve names to IDs here. |
| `conversations.info` | `channels:read` | `channel` | Channel metadata. |
| `conversations.members` | `channels:read` | `channel`, `cursor`, `limit` | Member IDs of a channel. |
| `conversations.create` | `channels:manage` | `name`, `is_private` | Create a channel. |
| `conversations.rename` | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `name` | Rename. |
| `conversations.archive` / `unarchive` | `channels:manage` | `channel` | Archive/unarchive. |
| `conversations.join` | `channels:join` | `channel` | Join a public channel. |
| `conversations.leave` | `channels:leave` | `channel` | Leave. |
| `conversations.invite` / `kick` | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `users` | Add/remove members (`users` is comma-separated IDs). |
| `conversations.setTopic` / `setPurpose` | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `topic`/`purpose` | Set topic/purpose. |
| `conversations.open` | `im:write` | `users`, `return_channel` | Open or resume a DM; returns the `im` channel ID. |
| `conversations.close` | `im:write` | `channel` | Close a DM/group DM. |

## Users

| method | scope | key params | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `users.list` | `users:read` | `cursor`, `limit` | All workspace members (default 100/page, max 200). |
| `users.info` | `users:read` | `user` | Profile + presence basics for one user. |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | `users:read.email` | `email` | Find a user by email. |
| `users.conversations` | `users:read` | `user`, `types`, `cursor` | Channels a user belongs to. |
| `users.getPresence` | `users:read` | `user` | `active` / `away`. |

## Reactions

| method | scope | key params | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reactions.add` | `reactions:write` | `channel`, `name`, `timestamp` | Emoji name without colons (e.g., `white_check_mark`). |
| `reactions.remove` | `reactions:write` | `channel`, `name`, `timestamp` | Remove a reaction. |
| `reactions.get` | `reactions:read` | `channel`, `timestamp` | Reactions on one message. |
| `reactions.list` | `reactions:read` | `user`, `cursor` | A user's recent reactions. |

## Files

| method | scope | key params | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files.upload` | `files:write` | `channels`, `content` or `file`, `filename`, `title`, `initial_comment`, `thread_ts` | **Multipart/form-data**, not JSON. Pass file content in `content` or use `file` for a multipart upload. |
| `files.info` | `files:read` | `file` | File metadata + download URL. |
| `files.list` | `files:read` | `channel`, `cursor`, `limit` | List files. |

## Search

| method | scope | key params | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search.messages` | `search:read` | `query`, `count`, `cursor` | Full-text message search. Supports the older `count`/`page` params too. |
| `search.files` | `search:read` | `query` | File search. |

## Workspace & token checks

| method | scope | key params | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auth.test` | none | — | Verify a token; returns `user_id`, `team_id`, `bot_id`. |
| `api.test` | none | — | Ping; returns `ok: true`. |
| `team.info` | `team:read` | — | Workspace name, domain, icon. |

## SDKs

For complex multi-step workflows, prefer an official SDK over raw HTTP:

- Node.js: `@slack/web-api` (`new WebClient(token)`)
- Python: `slack_sdk` (`WebClient(token)`)

Docs: https://api.slack.com/methods (method reference) and https://api.slack.com/docs/rate-limits (tiers).
